lots.guide_summary: All 9 surviving entries are SOLD Gowans hammer prices (AUD, no conversion) for boxes of wooden moulding planes in the last 12 months: $55 to $360, median $95. Boxes of 8-12 planes like this one made $80 to $95 (one at $230); $260 to $360 was for larger boxes of 15-20 planes or a named maker. No UNSOLD or ASKING evidence. Semmens book value not found (AbeBooks fetch returned no listings).
lots.working: keep: lowest same-size same-item SOLD = $90 (lots 377633 and 377652; the $55 lot 425212 was a smaller box and is excluded); 90 / 1.198 = 75.1, round down to $75. flip: likely resale about $120 (between the $95 median of close sales and the higher $230 result, discounted because no maker stamps are read), less 15% selling fees = $102, outbound postage $0 (sell locally, pickup); 102 / 2.396 = 42.6, round down to $40.
lots.confidence_reason: Clear identification and 9 opened SOLD comparables with photos checked, but maker stamps are not legible in the photo, so a named or Australian maker premium cannot be confirmed (High needs the mark read).
lots.condition: Used, dark patina, some grime; irons and wedges appear present in most planes; plough has brass-tipped wedge arms and a brass depth stop; no obvious breaks visible but the bodies are only partly seen.
lots.key_photo_findings: About 12 planes visible: mostly moulding planes, one wedge-arm plough with brass ferrules and brass diamond escutcheon, a fillister with a fence, a skew rebate, and a small coffin smoother at the top left. Book is Semmens 'Australian Woodworking Planemakers' second edition. No maker stamps legible on the toes at this resolution; a box with an Australian planemakers reference may mean Australian makers are present.
lots.question_for_gowans: Can you read any maker stamps on the plane toes (especially any Australian makers such as Hobart or Launceston names)? Are all irons and wedges present and are any bodies cracked?
